title: finalVerification runs on the phase-terminal node, never before
proves: finalVerificationCommands in final-verification.mjs appends contract.finalVerification to a node's own verification list only when phaseTerminalNode says no other node depends on it, and even then only once settledSiblingIds (computed fresh in engine/verify.mjs from every sibling's persisted status) reports every other phase-terminal node already settled: build has a dependant (ship), so it is never phase-terminal and its own taskPacket verification alone decides it, closing done before the phase's suite is ever considered — this pins the negative half (the suite never runs before the phase's last close). ship is the contract's only phase-terminal node, so by the time its own verification runs, build has already settled and the settled-siblings condition holds, so finalVerificationCommands appends the always-false command to ship's list and its otherwise-passing attempt settles as a verification failure — this pins the positive half (the suite does run, once, on the node that closes the phase). Removing contract.finalVerification entirely collapses the commands.length === 0 guard at the top of finalVerificationCommands, so no node's list ever gains the always-false command: ship's own true verification now passes unopposed and the run settles done/done instead of done/failed — a different outcome pair, exactly as dropping the field, mislaying it on build, or granting it before build's settled state was recorded each would produce.

contract.goal: prove finalVerification runs only on the phase-terminal node
